openingQuery: What linen do you have for 10 days in Goa?

chat.content: What linen do you have for 10 days in Goa?

Goa in linen - you'll want pieces that breathe, pack flat, and forgive a ten-day wear. Three I'd pull: the Hadley Linen Shirt in ivory ($248), the Linen Drawstring Trousers in oat ($178), and the Italian Linen Camp Shirt in indigo ($228). All three crumple honestly rather than crease - that's the tell of real linen, not a blend.

chat.content: What would go with the Hadley Linen Shirt?

The Hadley pairs beautifully with the Drawstring Trousers in oat - same washed-linen family, same tonal register, they read as a considered set rather than an accident. For layering when the evening cools, the Linen Overshirt in sage picks up the same muted palette without adding bulk. And the Leather Weekend Holdall ties the whole packing list together - the kind of bag that earns its patina on the trip.

chat.content: What's the price range for linen shirts?

Linen shirts in the catalog run from $88 to $285. Median is $148. The Hadley Linen Shirt ($248) and the Italian Linen Camp Shirt ($228) both sit in the upper third. Under $100 there are two - both cotton-linen blends rather than pure linen.

chat.content: How many Hadley Linen Shirts are available at the Brooklyn warehouse, and what ship window is recorded?

I can help with style and recommendations, but I don't have real-time stock visibility for individual warehouses yet. I can tell you the Hadley Linen Shirt is in the catalog and marked in-stock system-wide - but which warehouse holds it, and how many are on the floor, sits outside what I can answer right now.

sections.title: The arc
paragraphs: Marco arrived with a clear plan - ten days in Goa, linen - and walked through the catalog in four turns. Three landed cleanly. The fourth didn't.

The Dispatcher routed each turn to exactly one specialist: Search Agent on Claude Opus 4.6 for the opening ask, Personalization Agent on Claude Opus 4.6 with the-packing-list skill loaded for pairings, Pricing Agent on Claude Sonnet 4.6 for the price range. All three specialists running on their declared models; no normalization.

sections.title: The gap
paragraphs: Turn 4 - the warehouse-stock question - sits outside the system's current reach. The Dispatcher matched the intent, routed to Inventory Agent, and Inventory Agent answered with a voice-matched non-answer because the agent ships in stub state.
This is the workshop build. Participants complete the Inventory Agent definition and wire check_inventory. Once both are complete, the same Turn 4 pill returns a real warehouse + count + ETA.

sections.title: Why this matters
paragraphs: The gap isn't broken code. It's a design choice made visible: you only ship the agents you can answer for. Until Inventory Agent has real warehouse data behind it, the honest answer is 'I can't help with that yet.'
